figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. (A) The structures of compounds 1, 2, and 3 and other key products isolated in this study, see Figure S6 for all isolated compounds. (B)
Four possible diastereomers of compound 1. (C) The proposed biogenesis of the monomers of 1 and 3. An atrochrysone carboxylic acid (10)
derived xanthone ring contracts with loss of CO2 to form 9a, the precursor of 1, while the precursor of 3 would be from dehydration of scytalone, a
classical intermediate in the fungal DHN-melanin pathway. (D) HPLC analyses of extractions showing the biogenic crosstalk origin of compound
1.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. (A−C) Inhibitory potency of 1, 2, and 3 on LPS/ATP-induced IL-1β release in murine macrophage J774A.1 cells. (D,E) J774A.1 cells
were pretreated with indicated concentrations of tested compound 1 for 1 h and then supplemented with LPS (1 μg/mL) for 6 h. The levels of IL-6
and TNF-α were analyzed by ELISA. (F,G) J774A.1 cells were initially stimulated with LPS (1 μg/mL) and subsequently treated with compound 1
at 8.3 μM for 1 h. Subsequently, the cells were incubated with flagellin (1 μg/mL, used to activate NLRC4 inflammasome) for 6 h or poly(dA:dT)
(4 μg/mL, used to activate AIM2 inflammasome) for 8 h. The concentration of IL-1β in the supernatants was determined using ELISA analysis.
(H,I) The binding affinity of compound 1 to the human NLRP3 protein or human NLRP3 (mutated K232A) protein was assessed using a surface
plasmon resonance (SPR) assay. The KD values were calculated using Biacore evaluation software. The amino acid K232 is a crucial component of
the walker A motif located in the nucleotide-binding domain (NACHT), playing an essential role in ATPase activity. (J) Western blot analysis for
pro-caspase-1, and cleaved-caspase-1 (P20) in culture supernatants (SNs) and whole cell lysates (WCLs) in J774A.1 cells which stimulated by
LPS/ATP and treated with compound 1 and MCC950. (K) The prohealing function of compound 1 for diabetic wounds in vivo. Trace of wound
closure on days 0, 4, 6, 8, and 10. Scale bars, 4 mm. Data are shown as mean ± the standard error of the mean (SEM) and are representative of
three independent experiments. Statistics were analyzed by Student’s t-test, *p < 0.05. “NS” indicates no significant difference. The p-values refer to
the comparison between the vehicle and the treated group.
